_comment: The header values a network launch has to agree on. Each is a decision, not a
default — see docs/LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md §0 and §1.
genesis_time: the instant block 1 is stamped with. It must be a real UTC time in
the near future at launch, NOT the moment someone happened to run the build.
Emission is prorated against elapsed time, so a stale genesis pays the whole gap
out in one block — a day-old file once minted 125,485 ERTH at height 2. The
entrypoint currently rewrites this at boot, which is precisely why no two nodes
can share a chain; fixing that means setting a launch time here and stopping the
rewrite. The pol_burn schedules catch up the same way: a genesis four days old
retires four days of protocol-owned liquidity in one block. Measured, not
theoretical -- launching from this file today burns 2,996,952,143 LP shares at
height 2.
app_version is the launch app version. It moves with every coordinated upgrade,
and x/upgrade uses it to refuse a binary that is not the one the network agreed
to run.
block_max_gas caps how much gas one block may consume. The SDK default is -1,
meaning no cap at all: a block is bounded only by its 22MB size, so a single
transaction can consume as much gas as it likes and the per-node minimum fee is
the only brake on it. 100M is generous for normal use — a transfer is ~80k, a
passport registration much more because it verifies a proof — while still
stopping one transaction from taking a whole block. Governance can change it.
app_name / binary_version are the informational strings `earthd init` puts at the
top of the file. They are pinned here rather than taken from the build because a
genesis is only useful if it is byte-identical for everyone, and ldflags bake in
the git commit — the file would otherwise change every time anyone rebuilt it.
